## Summary

Adds `@ulugbekna` to `.github/CODENOTIFY` for the canvas implementation introduced in #338455 and the create-canvas skill.

Agent Host Protocol and session-list paths are intentionally excluded.

## Validation

- Passed: `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD`
- Passed: verified both notification patterns match tracked files
- Passed: verified no Agent Host Protocol or session-list paths are included

Scenarios.Scenario: Pull-request notification routing for changes under canvas implementation or create-canvas skill paths
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An external repository service may match changed file paths against CODENOTIFY and add the configured owner notification. No VS Code startup, rendering, input, extension execution, build, or test critical path reads this file in the repository.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potentially emit a GitHub notification/mention for @ulugbekna when a pull request touches either newly listed path family.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one newly configured owner per matching path family for a pull request; both rows target the same owner, so effective recipient cardinality is one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two path families had no explicit @ulugbekna CODENOTIFY entry, so this owner-specific external notification was not requested by these rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: External review notification routing is not on any shipped product critical path. Repository search found no in-repo consumer, so no product progress waits on this boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of files changed in a pull request and matching notification patterns. This diff adds exactly two glob patterns, each mapping to one owner; matching files under a pattern coalesce to the same owner rather than introducing per-product-item work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No repository implementation or concurrency mechanism references CODENOTIFY. Any matching and notification scheduling is owned by external GitHub infrastructure and is not changed in code here.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No repository cache is involved. Cold/warm matching behavior of the external notification service is not represented in the repository and the diff introduces no cache key, invalidation, miss retry, or retained cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff only adds two static metadata rows: the full changed-file inventory contains one file, its complete diff is 862 bytes, and repository-wide search found no CODENOTIFY consumer.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external service's implementation and exact deduplication policy are unavailable, but the changed configuration is statically bounded to two patterns and one recipient and cannot create repository runtime work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The only possible added boundary is a bounded external review notification, not a shipped product or repository-scale hot path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of the full one-file diff. Checked boundary fan-out, execution-path reachability, cardinality, caching, and concurrency. The two static notification mappings add no in-repository runtime, build, UI, IPC, filesystem, subprocess, or serialization work, and no valid performance finding was identified.
